To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake process influences the time‐course of the subsarcolemmal Ca2+ signal, which in turn activates ICl(CCa).
the mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake process is involved in regulating the time course of Ca2+ signals in the subsarcomplasmic domain of rabbit portal vein smooth muscles cells.

the time course of Ca2+activated Cl− currents is regulated by the rate of subsarcolemal Ca2+ clearance, which is controlled in part by the mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake mechanism, but not by the sarcolemmal Ca‐ATPase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Ca2+ signals in smooth muscle.
the modulation of Ca2+ activated chloride channels (ClC‐Ca) in vascular smooth muscle (VSMC) by the mitochondria.
the role of mitochondrial Ca2+-uptake processes in the regulation of Ca2+ transients and Ca2+-activated Cl- currents in smooth muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake is an important regulator of the Ca2+‐signal in the subsarcolema domain containing Ca2+-activated Cl− channels.
the time course of Ca2+ signal is regulated by Ca2+-dependent Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmatic reticulum and Ca2+ uptake in the mitochondria.
mitochondrial Ca2+ sequestration is a significant factor in the regulation of the Ca2+‐dependent chloride current in rabbit portal vein myocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time course of Ca2+ signals in the subsarcelemmal space is determined by the rate of Ca2+ influx, the rate of Ca‐dependent Cl− channel activation and the rate of mitochondrial Ca2 + uptake.
mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake regulates ICl(Ca) in rabbit portal vein cells.
the Ca2+‐induced Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmatic reticulum is not the major mechanism for the Ca2+ signal for the Ca2+-activated Cl− current in rabbit portal vein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial Ca2+ sequestration is an important regulator of the subsar-colemmal Ca2+-signalling domain that activates ICl,Ca.
mitochondrial Ca2+‐uptake regulates the subsarco­lemmal Ca2+-signal that activates Ca2+-activated Cl– channels in vascular smooth muscle.
the time‐dependent decay of ICl(CCa) in rabbit portal vein cells is modulated by mitochondrial Ca2+ sequestration.
